Second alpha. The project was consolidated into one codebase and the git history squashed; this is the first release built by CI.

## Play
Download the archive for your OS, unpack, run `ai-evolve` (`ai-evolve.exe` on Windows). The hero is AI-controlled; you are the level director:

- **1 / 2 / 3** — spawn an enemy / trap / chest next to the hero
- **Space / left mouse** — force an attack
- **Esc** — quit

The standalone build starts on the small dev map; run with `--full` for the full-size world. Logs are written to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-EVOLVE\output.log` (Windows) or the equivalent user data folder.

## What's new since v0.1.x
- Main menu (Russian UI), then the game world; boot goes through GameCore → SceneManager → plugins.
- Effects in combat: buffs/debuffs change combat stats, elite/boss hits slow, stealth attacks poison, damage-over-time respects death.
- Hero levels up from kills, opened chests and disarmed traps; enemies get stronger over time.
- `rust_core` (PyO3 0.29, Lua 5.5) builds on Windows, Linux and macOS; wheels for Python 3.14 are attached. The game itself does not use it yet; the developer tools below use it for analytics when it is installed.
- Python 3.14.
- Tooling: headless combat and boot tests in CI; `tools/dev_probe.py` now reports FAIL when the world is empty, frames are blank or errors are logged.

## Developer & QA tooling (source checkout only, not in the game archives)
Built so that AI agents (and people) can test the game with far less reading. Start with `CLAUDE.md` and `python tools/qa.py brief`; the audit of the old probe is in `docs/DEV_PROBE_AUDIT.md`.
- `tools/agent_play.py` — play with the player's own controls (spawn enemy/trap/chest, attack, interact) plus `wait / until / observe / expect / story`, with no window and no GPU. A fixed-step virtual clock makes runs about 200x faster than real time and byte-for-byte reproducible; every failing run prints a one-line `repro:` command. `--serve` allows turn-based play over HTTP.
- `tools/dev_probe.py` — `--render offscreen|none` and `--fast`; rule-based hypotheses ("symptom → likely cause → file") and forecasts in `summary.md`; the sound is muted, so about 40 lines of ALSA noise are gone from every run. It also no longer crashes at the end when OpenCV is installed.
- `tools/probe_db.py` — every run lands in SQLite: `stats` (per enemy type, hit/crit/dodge, time-to-kill), `why`, `predict`, `compare`, `trend`, `sql`.
- `tools/qa.py` — one command per question: `test` runs pytest in parallel shards and prints only new failures (flaky ones are detected automatically). `golden` checks deterministic gameplay scenarios, `fuzz` hunts bugs with random player actions and per-frame invariants and shrinks each bug to a minimal script, and `sweep` runs a scenario over many seeds (Monte Carlo with confidence intervals). `affected`, `ctx`, `dead`, `docs`, `perf` and `doctor` are also there.
- Rust kernels (`RunAnalytics`, `QaKernels`) take column buffers from Python in one FFI call. They are about 13x faster than Python on the analysis and 170x faster on bootstrap statistics, and each has a Python twin that gives the same results.
- Thresholds, scenarios and player key bindings for the tools live in Lua (`lua_content/dev_tools.lua`, `lua_content/qa.lua`).
- The whole test suite runs in about 4 s instead of 72 s: timer-based tests use a manual clock and run in parallel shards. The training room now actually loads `mannequins.lua` and no longer writes into tracked folders.

## Fixed with the help of the new tools
- The hero's HP could exceed its maximum (e.g. 149/120) after the first hit, and health regen was lost on the next hit: `HealthComponent` was created before the class set `max_health`. The two now stay in sync.
- The hero got stuck in `seeking_exit` after walking to the first point of the echo trail and stood there forever. Now it follows the trail to the exit and advances levels.
- Training room: "+20% strength" was computed from the already buffed strength (20 → 24). Event bonuses such as Vampire's Fang also piled up with every hit instead of tracking kills.
- Lost My Self (Sorrow of Berserk) now matches the design:
  - crit chance, crit damage and lifesteal are added in points;
  - the Last Will shield makes you invulnerable for 5 s, with a 30 s cooldown and +5 s per kill;
  - at exactly 1 HP every bonus doubles per missing 10% (x8).

  The item is defined in `lua_content/items/sorrow_of_berserk.lua`, and `tests/test_lost_my_self_spec.py` checks it against the design.

## Known issues
- On the dev map, enemies spawn about 160 units from the hero, so a run without director spawns (1/2/3) often has no combat at all.
- The balance heavily favours the hero right now: the hero hits for up to about 285 damage against 50 HP enemies, while enemies hit for about 2.

## Known limitations
- The hero's "learning" is still rule-based; counter-learning and enemy collective memory are next.
- Crowd control, toughness/stagger, item effects and the full damage pipeline (resistances, block, accuracy, penetration) exist in code but are not wired into the game yet.
- Only the Windows build was run by hand; the Linux and macOS builds come from CI and are untested on real machines. The macOS app is unsigned (right-click → Open the first time).
